clue.text: Party official carries note to copier for policy proposal

indicators.note: the official carries a note, so the note sits inside the official's title

parts.note: a whip is the party official who enforces discipline among MPs
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
an aper is one who apes, that is copies

explanation.surface: A party functionary takes a memo to the photocopier so a policy proposal can be duplicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copier' looks like an office machine, but here it is APER, someone who apes another.
explanation.definitionFit: A government white paper is a document setting out proposed policy before legislation.

clue.text: Resolute advocate of reliable intercontinental transport

parts.note: hard, as in hard facts or hard evidence, means solid and dependable
an ocean liner carries passengers between continents

explanation.surface: Someone champions dependable long-distance travel between continents.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sticks rigidly to an uncompromising position is a resolute advocate of it.

clue.text: Flavouring of the hour, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: an hour is a time, as in 'at what hour?'

explanation.surface: A seasoning that is fashionable right now, the flavour of the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the hour' suggests a fashion; 'of' is only a link, and the hour gives TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is a herb used as a culinary seasoning.

clue.text: Social event, with everything that may be shared between neighbours

definitions.text: that may be shared between neighbours

parts.note: a party is a social gathering
all means everything

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood get-together where everyone shares everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A party wall is a dividing wall jointly owned by two adjoining properties.

clue.text: Missing song, play recent or old record?

indicators.note: the play is missing a song, so those letters are taken out of the word

parts.note: a lay is a song or ballad
latter means more recent, as in latter days

explanation.surface: A DJ, lacking a requested song, wonders whether to spin something new or something old.
explanation.walkthrough: PLAY without LAY leaves P; add LATTER. The question mark flags that 'record' is old slang for a gramophone disc.
explanation.definitionFit: Platter is dated slang for a gramophone record.

clue.text: Gas not quite random in movement

indicators.note: the remaining letters are set in motion, rearranged into a new order
not quite the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A gas whose molecules drift about almost randomly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' cuts M from 'random' to leave RANDO, which 'in movement' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive noble gas, element 86.

clue.text: Lying at last in shade is great

indicators.note: the letter is placed in the shade, inside the word for colour

parts.note: a hue is a shade of colour

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of lying

explanation.surface: Lounging in the shade at the end of the day is wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge and great are synonyms for very large in size.

clue.text: Something in beer and spirit creates childish amusement

parts.note: the hop is the plant whose flowers flavour beer
Scotch whisky is a spirit

explanation.surface: Mixing beer and whisky leads to juvenile behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a children's playground game of hopping between squares.

clue.text: Wife secured by chap in part of Wales once

indicators.note: the wife is held fast by the chap, so she goes inside his word

parts.note: a gent is a man or chap

explanation.surface: A Welshman of old holds on to his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Gwent was a Welsh county from 1974 to 1996, and earlier a medieval kingdom.

clue.text: Pensioners' field that's not properly marked out

parts.note: grey describes the elderly, as in the grey vote
a field of study or activity is an area

explanation.surface: Retirees' land without clear boundary markings.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey area is a situation with no clear rules, a zone without defined limits.

clue.text: Bird that may be big in sky

definitions.meaning: a small songbird that feeds in streams

definitions.text: that may be big in sky
definitions.meaning: the star pattern also called the Plough

explanation.surface: A bird that looms large overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: The dipper is a river bird, and the Big Dipper is a constellation shape.

clue.text: Nodding, Prime Minister's given backing to unknown

indicators.note: given backing means the word is read in reverse order

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was a 19th-century British Prime Minister; with the 's that gives PEELS
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A dozing Prime Minister has endorsed a mystery candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodding off, someone is drowsy and on the verge of sleep.

clue.text: Doggedness shown by a few from each large town

parts.note: ten is taken as a small number, a few
a, as in 'a pound a head', means per or from each
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Persistence displayed by a handful of people from every big town.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenacity is persistent determination, the quality of holding on.

clue.text: Disadvantage of combining two metals

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Merging two metals has a downside.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a drawback or unexpected problem.

clue.text: Time to take piano on — our noble attempt at cultural improvement

parts.note: a grand is a grand piano

explanation.surface: It is time to haul the piano along on our high-minded cultural trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time to take piano on' places T after GRAND, which it takes on in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand Tour was the educational journey through Europe made by young aristocrats.

clue.text: What one may see in circus act, basic or special

definitions.text: What one may see in circus

indicators.note: special suggests something made out of the ordinary, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Musings on whether a circus turn is ordinary or remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges the letters of 'act basic or'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrobatics, tumbling and balancing feats, are a staple of the circus ring.

clue.text: Beat up thoroughly, though without conviction

parts.note: to bash is to beat up
fully means thoroughly or completely

explanation.surface: Someone gives a thrashing but half-heartedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting shyly and diffidently is acting without self-assurance or conviction.

clue.text: So purgative, as girl goes to far north to get rid of a cold

parts.note: Cath is a girl's name, short for Catherine

indicators.note: the far north gets rid of the cold, so its letter is dropped

parts.note: the Arctic is the far north
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A girl heads to the Arctic hoping to shake off a cold, as a kind of purge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get rid of' drops one C from the far north; 'goes to' and 'as' are only links, and 'So' leans on the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathartic means cleansing, a medicine that purges the bowels.

clue.text: Fear prison will be a graet shock

parts.note: dread means fear
locks, in the sense of locks up, means imprisons

explanation.surface: Fear of jail will be a big fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'graet' is the paper's own typo for 'great'. 'shock' is a thick mass of hair, not a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadlocks are long matted ropes of hair, a great shock of hair.

clue.text: Slave, defence cut short, put in prison

indicators.note: the shortened defence is put in the prison, inside its word

parts.note: can is slang for prison

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is removed

parts.note: an alibi is a defence that one was elsewhere

explanation.surface: A slave whose legal defence was curtailed is jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Caliban is the enslaved creature in Shakespeare's The Tempest.

clue.text: Hot to get vengeance, feeling this?

definitions.text: Hot to get vengeance, feeling this?

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and vengeance

explanation.surface: Someone burning for revenge wonders what emotion this is.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatred is the emotion of someone burning for revenge.

clue.text: In favour of new style of TV — missing it is reckless

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: the TV style is missing the word 'it', so those letters are removed

parts.note: digital television replaced analogue broadcasting

explanation.surface: Backing new digital television, going without it is foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing it' strips those two letters from the TV style; the dash separates wordplay from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigal means wastefully extravagant, as with the prodigal son.

clue.text: Brainless hero in word-game losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: crambo is a rhyming word game

explanation.surface: A dim-witted protagonist flounders at a word game.
explanation.definitionFit: Rambo is the brawny film action hero, a byword for muscle over brains.

clue.text: Devise elaborate costume

definitions.meaning: to ... a scheme is to organise or devise it
a ... is an outfit, often a showy one

explanation.definitionFit: Get up means arrange or contrive; a getup is a striking costume.

clue.text: Rich man's pampered pet

definitions.meaning: a wealthy, privileged person, especially a well-paid executive

explanation.definitionFit: Fat cat is slang for a wealthy, privileged person; literally it is an overfed moggy.

clue.text: Scent to follow either side of river

indicators.note: the following word goes on either side of the river, enclosing it

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: A dog picks up a scent and follows it along both banks of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail is the track or scent left by a quarry, followed by hounds.

clue.text: I pay upfront, caught by over 50% tax

indicators.note: the letter is caught by the larger word, so it goes inside

parts.note: most means more than half

indicators.note: upfront points to the first letter of pay

explanation.surface: Someone pays in advance and gets hit by a tax of more than half.
explanation.definitionFit: An impost is a tax or duty levied, especially on imports.

clue.text: Deficient in decibel, can't opera be sung like this?

indicators.note: the run is short of the full words, sitting inside them with their ends lost

explanation.surface: Could opera be sung quietly, lacking volume?
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside 'decibel, can't opera'; the def leans on 'opera' just before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bel canto is the lyrical, smooth Italian operatic singing style.

clue.text: Land mainly high but low by river

parts.note: to low is to moo like cattle

explanation.surface: Terrain that is largely upland yet lies low beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like the opposite of high, but it is a cow's moo.
explanation.definitionFit: A moor is an expanse of open, usually high, uncultivated land.

clue.text: Today one would be unlikely to lick this girl chessplayer

definitions.text: Today one would be unlikely to lick this

parts.note: Penny is a girl's name
Black is one of the two players in chess

explanation.surface: A girl who plays chess is hardly someone you would lick nowadays.
explanation.definitionFit: The Penny Black, the first adhesive postage stamp of 1840, is now too valuable to lick.
